text:
sam: seeing ALB mark 3 targets UNHEALTHY and then remove them in us-west-2-edge at ~10:12. pods are Ready in k8s. ALB event says connection reset during health check. Anyone seen similar?
zhang: I pulled the ALB access logs, here's a representative line: 
```
2026-07-14T10:12:13.123Z elb target:10.0.12.34:8080 elb_status_code=504 target_status_code=0 reason='TCP_RESET' bytes_received=0 bytes_sent=0
```
leah: quick checks: kubectl get pods on those nodes -> Ready=1/1. curl directly to pod IP from jumpbox returns 200 and small body. So app responds.
sam: also saw a bunch of `Connection reset by peer` in node dmesg around same time. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT/GW causing ALB->target TCP flows to reset?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: noticed a config push to edge-proxy 10:09 UTC (revision r243).
zhang: checked conntrack on node-ops (one of the nodes in the target group): `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` -> ~61000 entries for TCP. `cat /proc/sys/net/nf_conntrack_max` -> 65536. That margin is tight.
leah: AWS NAT gateway metrics for the account/az show ActiveConnections ~= 62000 and PortAllocation nearing limit for a single Elastic IP. NAT GW with 1 EIP will run out of ephemeral ports and start resetting flows. ALB healthchecks to pod IPs can be affected when ALB's path goes through NAT path for some setups.
sam: interesting -- these are IP targets (targets are pod IPs). If ALB healthchecks originate from its nodes and hit pod IPs, they should be direct, but our egress topology puts a sidecar proxy on node that SNATs outbound, and we also have some cross-subnet hairpin via NAT in this AZ. messy.
leah: short-term mitigation options: 1) increase ALB health check timeout to 10s and unhealthy threshold to 3 to avoid flapping, 2) add additional NAT gateway/EIPs to spread port allocation, 3) switch target group to instance targets (NodePort) so LB -> node -> kube-proxy -> pod avoids SNAT, 4) reduce conntrack TTL by tuning net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established (risky).
zhang: I pushed a temporary change: increased health check timeout from 5 -> 8s and unhealthy threshold 2 -> 4 for the edge target group. Also created a second NAT gateway in the same AZ and attached new EIP to route table, will validate metrics.
sam: thanks. for triage: can someone run `sudo conntrack -S` during the flaps and capture `tcp` stats and `ss -s`? also put ALB access logs for the period in S3.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. scaling NAT GW now and will monitor port allocation and ALB target health. will also coordinate with edge-proxy team about switching to instance targets in a followup change.
sam: one more note — we should add an alert on conntrack % usage on nodes and ActiveConnections per NAT GW to prevent surprise. :eyes:
leah: Agreed. I'll open a short RFC for long-term: prefer instance targets for stable healthchecks + ensure NAT autoscale or add EIPs.
zhang: follow-up: after adding NAT + bumped healthchecks the target group stabilized at 10:40 and no further deregistrations. Monitoring for 1h.
oncall-sre: resolved for now, will keep ticket open. :white_check_mark:
